name: Available Power, LLC (a business unit of Available Infrastructure)
headquarters: Parent Available Infrastructure: Tysons Corner, Northern Virginia ('along the Washington, DC, beltway'); Available Power releases were datelined Austin, Texas (2022) and Boulder, Colorado (2023) — no street address is published
employees: Not disclosed; the parent's team page lists 29 names (September 2026), three of them tagged Available Power; The Org lists the unit at '1-10 employees'
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Available Power is not a CAISO/ERCOT merchant storage specialist and, on the public record, owns no operating battery. It is a Texas-only developer that sells distribution-connected 9.9 MW / 20 MWh batteries and one 100 MW / 200 MWh transmission-connected project at notice-to-proceed — 'we sell the projects at NTP' (VP Business Development Alex Krass, April 2023) — with Linxon, the Hitachi Energy and AtkinsRéalis joint venture, as the turnkey EPC that carries the asset to operation for a financial buyer. No sponsor, fund, lender, tax-equity investor or offtaker is named in any release, filing or article read; the only dollar figure attached to the storage business is Stem's February 2022 statement that a 100-site, 1 GW / 2 GWh Texas portfolio was 'expected to have a value of more than $500 million'. The last storage-side disclosure is March 2024 — Greenport (Bastrop County, ERCOT) 'at NTP' and being auctioned through LevelTen with a February 2026 operating date, and 'three assets' of 9.9 MW 'recently sold' to unnamed buyers. Since July 2025 the parent trades as Available Infrastructure, a Northern Virginia edge-AI and zero-trust cybersecurity company (SanQtum, a '$5 billion Project Qestrel' of 1,000 micro data centres with IBM, Crown Castle and Datavault AI), and 'Available Power' is one of its two business units; nothing ties the micro data centres to Texas batteries.

BACKGROUND. Founded in early 2020 by brothers Daniel Gregory (CEO, ex-Shell head of microgrid solutions) and Benjamin Gregory (President, ex-Shell) with Hervé Touati (Executive Chairman, ex-Shell New Energies and first CEO of the Energy Web Foundation), the company described itself as 'a pure-play developer bringing de-risked, investment-grade assets to the modern power grid', partnering 'with real estate portfolio owners to site distributed energy systems such as batteries' on leased land, 'currently focused on the Texas market'. Milestones: Stem selected to supply hardware and Athena software for up to 100 front-of-meter sites (February 2022); the 100 MW / 200 MWh Greenport project at the proposed GREENPORT International Airport and Technology Center near Austin (September 2022, commercial 'mid-2024', then Q1 2025, then February 2026); a Linxon strategic partnership on a '1,000+ megawatt' ERCOT pipeline, 'an estimated 75%' of it distribution-connected at 'an average size of 10 MW / 20 MWh' (February 2023), and Linxon's exclusivity agreement for Greenport's 345 kV substation and balance of plant (May 2023); a joint venture with CleanCapital, which was to bring 'project financing, development, and construction expertise' (February 2024). Revenue on the batteries was described as merchant — energy trading plus ERCOT responsive-reserve and fast-frequency-response services.

Collection gap: the corporate site's storage pages are gone (available-power.com now redirects to the parent; the 'what we do' and 'Bedrock' pages return 404), the Wayback Machine is unreachable from this environment, and no buyer of any Available Power project has ever been named by either side. The premise handed to this dossier is corrected on geography (Texas, not California), model (develop-and-sell, not owner-operator), sponsor (none named) and status (no operating fleet documented). Cleanview's September 2026 ERCOT operating list and Modo Energy's February 2026 owner report do not name Available Power.
ecosystemRole: Available Power is the corpus's example of the sub-10 MW 'distributed play' in ERCOT — batteries sized just under the threshold at which a project must enter ERCOT's full interconnection study, sited on leased commercial land, packaged with an EPC and sold at notice-to-proceed to financial buyers who own but do not develop. It sits upstream of owners like GridStor and Spearmint in the value chain and, since 2025, inside a parent whose business is edge data centres rather than power.

productsAndServices.name: Distribution-connected 9.9 MW / 20 MWh batteries — developed to notice-to-proceed and sold
productsAndServices.description: The core product: two-hour lithium-ion batteries of 9.9 MW on leased real-estate sites in Texas, sized under 10 MW so that, in Krass's words, 'you can skip a part of the interconnection process with ERCOT ... so your time to market is quicker'. Linxon's February 2023 release put the pipeline at '1,000+ megawatt' with 'an estimated 75%' distribution-connected at an average 10 MW / 20 MWh; Energy-Storage.news in April 2023 described 300 MW / 600 MWh of near-term projects — Greenport plus 'ten 9.9MW projects' — expected to reach NTP in 2023 and operate in 2024. The company sells at NTP 'but with the Linxon relationship, we have the contracts, the equipment procured and everything in place, so it's sort of a turnkey approach to the asset buyer', targeting 'traditional financial capital partners versus someone who might have an EPC relationship'. By March 2024 'the firm recently sold three assets this size'; buyers, prices and counties were never disclosed.
highlights: Krass (April 2023): 'Two hour duration is the sweet spot ... going to three or four you really get hammered on the Capex'

Gregory (March 2024): a 'manufacturing-like, standardised approach to development ... we might leave some money on the table but we can do much more volume'; 'A project that was at 12% IRR last year, is now at 14-15% IRR because of the BESS price falls'

Stem (February 2022): exclusive rights to supply Athena software at 100 front-of-meter Texas sites, hardware included, 'beginning with deployment of the first 20 systems by early 2023'; no delivery was ever reported

Peer set for the sub-10 MW segment per Energy-Storage.news (March 2026): Bimergen (eight 9.9 MW projects bought from Aggreko), GoodPeak, ON.energy, Plus Power — Available Power is cited only for its 2023 interconnection quote
productsAndServices.positioning: A volume developer of small standardised units where Spearmint, GridStor and Aypa build 100–400 MW transmission-connected projects; the edge is speed through the distribution interconnection path and a repeatable site-lease template, the cost is a buyer base of financial owners who need a turnkey EPC attached.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Sale at notice-to-proceed to financial buyers, with Linxon as EPC and equipment procurer carrying construction to operation; land leased from 'real estate portfolio owners'; merchant ERCOT revenue thereafter for the buyer.
targetSegments: Infrastructure funds and financial owners without EPC relationships
productsAndServices.roadmap: None published since March 2024; the parent's news archive since then contains no storage release.

productsAndServices.name: Greenport BESS — 100 MW / 200 MWh transmission-connected project
productsAndServices.category: Development — utility-scale BESS (at NTP, offered for sale)
productsAndServices.description: Announced 7 September 2022 with GREENPORT Energy: a 100 MW / 200 MWh front-of-meter lithium-ion battery on leased land at the proposed GREENPORT International Airport and Technology Center on the Colorado River about 15–17 miles from downtown Austin (Bastrop County per the airport's own materials), interconnecting at 345 kV; 'ground breaking late 2023, commercial deployment mid-2024'. Linxon's May 2023 exclusivity agreement covers 'a 345/34.5kV, 130 MVA step-up power transformer, 345kV AIS equipment, battery enclosures, inverter skid with coupling transformer, inverter control system/EMS, and station auxiliary supply system', with completion 'by Q1 2025'. In March 2024 Ben Gregory said 'Greenport is at NTP, and we're currently selling the project ... running an auction process, in coordination with LevelTen Energy', with equipment secured for a February 2026 operating date. No sale, financing, energisation or commissioning has been reported by any party since, and the airport campus itself 'remains unapproved with no scheduled construction date' per community-meeting coverage.
highlights: The host campus was marketed as a home for data centres, research and 'government agencies with high-security requirements', with a biofuel combined-cycle plant 'that will eventually generate 800 MW' — the battery was grid-facing, not a behind-the-meter contract
Revenue model as described in 2022: wholesale energy plus ERCOT responsive reserve service and fast frequency response — no offtaker
Battery supplier never named: the Sungrow photograph in the March 2024 Energy-Storage.news article is captioned as another company's Texas project
productsAndServices.positioning: The one transmission-scale project in a distribution-scale portfolio, and the only named asset; its fate is the test of whether the develop-and-sell model closed at 100 MW.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Auction through the LevelTen Energy project marketplace (March 2024); Linxon EPC exclusivity attached.
targetSegments: Project buyers in the pre-COD ERCOT market
productsAndServices.roadmap: Stated operating date February 2026; no confirmation exists.

productsAndServices.name: CleanCapital joint venture and the parent's edge data-centre business
productsAndServices.description: In February 2024 Available Power and CleanCapital formed a joint venture 'for storage development' in which CleanCapital would 'provide project financing, development, and construction expertise' and Available Power 'market insights, technology, and engineering expertise to develop strategically located batteries' in Texas and 'emerging markets across the U.S.'; CleanCapital's near-term storage pipeline was 'over 500 MWh' and no JV capitalisation was disclosed. No project has been attributed to the venture since. From July 2025 the parent — Available Infrastructure, 'parent company to Available Networks and Available Power subsidiaries' — has issued only cybersecurity and edge-AI releases: SanQtum (July 2025), a US patent for a firewall gateway protecting distributed energy resources and EV charging (July 2025), IBM offering the product as SanQtum AI (December 2025), and Project Qestrel — 'nearly $5 billion in project CapEx at full buildout', 1,000 micro data-centre sites in 100 US cities with up to 48 GPUs each, with Crown Castle, IBM, Strata Expanse, RAVEL and Datavault AI (March 2026). Datavault AI's Q2 2026 results record SanQtum deployments in New York and Philadelphia and that no tokens had been sold for the announced '$QEST' tokenisation.
highlights: CEO Dan Gregory (September 2026): the company 'was originally founded with an early focus on the energy sector, including minigrids, virtual power plants, and battery energy storage systems'
No release states that Available Power batteries supply or back the micro data-centre sites
productsAndServices.positioning: A developer whose parent has moved its capital and identity to a different infrastructure class; for a storage supplier the unit is a dormant counterparty until a new project appears.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Joint-venture development (CleanCapital); parent-level partnerships (IBM, Crown Castle, Datavault AI).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Project Qestrel: '30 cities online by early July 2026' and nationwide by end-2026 per the parent; no storage roadmap.

policyExposure.regime: ERCOT distribution-connected generation rules (sub-10 MW path)
policyExposure.exposure: The business model rests on ERCOT's treatment of resources under 10 MW: 'you can skip a part of the interconnection process with ERCOT (with projects under 10MW) so your time to market is quicker' (Krass, April 2023); the company's pipeline was '75%' distribution-connected at 'an average size of 10 MW / 20 MWh' for that reason. Krass also said 'a lot of the PUCTs regulations coming in are incentivising the 2-hour-plus duration'.

Available Power described its batteries' revenue as merchant — wholesale energy plus responsive reserve service and fast frequency response — in an energy-only market with no capacity payment. ERCOT's RTC+B redesign went live on 5 December 2025, modelling batteries as single state-of-charge resources; Modo Energy reports two-hour batteries out-earned one-hour units by 15–81 per cent in 2026, which favours the company's two-hour template.

Non-residential storage keeps the full 48E investment tax credit through 2033 under the July 2025 law, which underwrites the pre-COD value of projects sold at notice-to-proceed; Available Power never disclosed a credit transfer, tax-equity investor or lender, so how its buyers monetised the credit is unknown.

The prohibited-foreign-entity material-assistance rules apply to storage projects beginning construction from 2026, with non-PFE cost ratios rising from 55 per cent (2026) to 75 per cent (2030) per Foley Hoag's July 2026 summary; any Available Power project not yet under construction — Greenport had equipment 'secured' in March 2024 but no reported start — would be tested against them. No company statement on FEOC exists.

SB 6 defines large loads at 75 MW and above and gives ERCOT curtailment and co-location review powers over them (PURA §39.169 and §39.170 per Baker Botts); Available Power's distribution-scale batteries sit below every SB 6 threshold, and the parent's micro data centres, at up to 48 GPUs a site, are far below the large-load line — the law is context, not an exposure.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Available Power is a Texas-only develop-and-sell developer of distribution-connected batteries, not an owner-operator and not a CAISO participant, and that the premise handed to this dossier is wrong on geography, model and sponsor. Basis: every company and partner release says 'currently focused on the Texas market'; the VP Business Development said 'we sell the projects at NTP'; no CAISO project, offtaker, toll or hedge appears anywhere; no fund or investor is named by any source.

(High confidence) We assess that no battery is operating under Available Power's ownership and that the storage business has been publicly dormant since March 2024. Basis: the last storage disclosure is the March 2024 interview; the parent's news archive from then to September 2026 contains no storage item; Modo Energy's 2025 ERCOT owner report and Cleanview's September 2026 operating list do not name the company; the three 9.9 MW sales and the Greenport auction have no reported outcome.

(High confidence) We assess that the parent has redirected its identity and capital to edge micro data centres and cybersecurity, with Available Power retained as a business unit rather than a growth line. Basis: the July 2025 rebrand to Available Infrastructure in Tysons Corner, the patent, IBM and Datavault AI releases, and the March 2026 'Project Qestrel' plan; the CEO's September 2026 description of energy as the company's 'early focus'.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the sub-10 MW template was sound on its own terms — the segment it described in 2023 is now populated by Bimergen, GoodPeak, ON.energy and Plus Power, and ERCOT's RTC+B rewards two-hour duration — and that the company's problem was the buyer side, not the product. Basis: Gregory's own statement that price falls lifted project IRRs to '14–15%' while the firm was still auctioning Greenport; the CleanCapital JV's stated purpose was to supply 'project financing'. Cuts against: the absence of any named buyer means the sales themselves cannot be verified.

(Low confidence) Greenport may have been sold and built under another name: the March 2024 statement that equipment was 'secured' for a February 2026 operating date is consistent with a completed sale, but no ERCOT record, buyer release or trade-press item found confirms it, and the host airport campus remains unapproved. Treat the project as status unknown.

Collection gap: the company's own storage pages are gone and the Wayback Machine is unreachable from this environment, so the 2022–2024 record is reconstructed from partner releases and two Energy-Storage.news interviews; no queue identifier, permit, abatement, lender or buyer could be found. Indicators to watch: (1) an ERCOT commercial-operations or Cleanview entry for a 100 MW / 200 MWh battery in Bastrop County — that would resolve Greenport's fate; (2) any release from a financial owner naming Available Power as the seller of a 9.9 MW portfolio — the first would confirm the sales were real; (3) a storage-related release from Available Infrastructure, or a project attributed to the CleanCapital JV — either would show the unit is active; (4) a Datavault AI or parent disclosure tying Project Qestrel sites to on-site batteries — that would reconnect the two businesses; (5) the Bastrop County airport's approval status — the host campus is the precondition for the only named project.
